full_judgment:
K M Hasan J: The Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order passed by the respondent No. 2 in Appeal Case No. 51 of 1997 dated 2-4-97 vide Annexure-G affirming the order dated 23-3-97 passed by the respondent No. 3 in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1997 vide Annexure-D should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 2. The facts, in short, as stated in the petition, are that, the respondent No. 4, Thana Nirbahi Officer, Kushtia Sadar, Kushtia by advertisement issued in "Dainik Kushtia" and "The Andoloner Bazar" invited tender from interested parties for lease of Ailchara Cattle Market by auction, the last date of purchase of schedule was 24-2-97 and time for submitting the tender was fixed till 2-00 PM on 25-2-97. Accordingly, the petitioner purchased the tender schedule, deposited the earnest money amounting to Taka 5,00,000.00 and submitted the tender before 2 PM on 25-2-97 with an offer to purchase the said Ailchara Caule Market at Taka 9,65,500.00. When the tender box was opened, he was found by the authority to be the highest bidder and his offer was accepted. On the same day after 2-00 PM one Shahabul Alam filed an application in plain paper before the Thana Nirbahi Officer, Kushtia offering an amount of Taka 9,75;500.00 for taking lease of the said cattle market. He had also stated that he could not put the schedule in the tender box at the appointed time as it was snatched away by some miscreants, The authority then asked the petitioner whether he was ready to offer an amount of Taka 9,75,500.00 which was equivalent to the amount offered by Shahabul Alam. As the petitioner expressed his desire to purchase the same, by paying the said amount the authority accepted the proposal and directed the petitioner to deposit the rest amount The petitioner deposited the rest bringing the total amount deposited to Taka 9,75,500.00 as per direction of the authority and also deposited the income tax, VAT, etc. amounting to Taka 29,265.00 (Annexures A and B). Thereafter, a lease deed was executed between the petitioner and the respondent No. 4 representing the President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (Annexure-C). 

 4.The petitioner then preferred an Appeal Case No. 51 of 1997 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner. Khulna against the order of the Deputy Commissioner. The Additional Deputy Commissioner, Khulna by his order dated 2-4-97 disallowed the appeal and upheld the order of the Deputy Commissioner (Annexure-F), 

 7. Respondent NO.5 Md. Shahabul Alam who was added as respondent No. 5 by an order of this Court on 30-4-97, by filing an affidavit-in-opposition, denied all the material allegations and has further submitted that on 25-2-97 while he was going to the office of the Thana Nirbahi Officer to drop the tender schedule before the appointed time the tender papers were snatched away from him by some miscreants. He reported the matter to the Thana Nirbahi Officer and filed an application before 2-00 PM on the same date with a CD of Taka 5 lakh. In this application he offered Taka 9,75,000.00 to take lease of the said cattle market but at 2-30 PM of the same date when the tender box was opened, apart from his written application, only one schedule was found which was dropped by the petitioner. In this connection he has further stated that four tender schedules were sold by the respondent No. 4 but only one was dropped. He claimed that tender money in the form of CD was paid by his business associates on his behalf, so there is nothing wrong in it. As his offer was not accepted the respondent No. 5 filed Miscellaneous Case before the Deputy Commissioner, Kushtia praying that a re-tender should be called on the ground that he was the highest bidder but it was not accepted and the market was leased to the petitioner in a malafide manner. In this connection he has stated that the lease amount offered by the petitioner was less than the lease money received by the Government in previous years as for example in the year, 1400 BS the cattle market was leased for Taka 17,76,000:00, in the year 1401 it was leased for Taka 10,50,000.00 and in the year 1402 BS the lease money received was Taka 10,25,000.00. Therefore he prayed for a fresh tender before the Deputy Commissioner with a proposal that he is ready to raise the bid to Taka 13,50,000.00 if re-tender was called. The Deputy Commissioner by his order dated 23-3-97 cancelled the lease and the lease agreement by the petitioner and directed for a fresh re-tender of the cattle market and asked the respondent to deposit Taka 13,50,000.00 in advance. Accordingly respondent No. 5 deposited the said amount by CD with the respondent No. 4 the Thana Nirbahi Officer (Annexures 1, 2, 3 and 4). 

 9. Dr Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has submitted that the petitioner is vested with interest of the cattle market by execution of the lease agreement and therefore, his right cannot be taken away without giving him a notice or a hearing. He has further submitted that a re-tender could have been called before the execution of the lease deed but once the lease deed was executed the re-tender should not have been called in the absence of violation of any term and condition of the lease agreement. In this connection he has referred to the case of Sonali Fishermen's Co-operative Society Ltd. vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 46 DLR 402 wherein it has been held "Unless the lessee had violated any condition the Government cannot arbitrarily cancel the lease agreement." Then he referred us to Rule (Uma) of Government Hat and Bazar, and Management Rules issued by Local Government Division. According to which the tender of the highest bidders should be accepted but the amount offered should be more than the average-of previous year's lease money. The petitioner's bidding was more than the previous years lease money which was Taka 5,55,000.00 and the average of the last three years lease money for the same cattle market. He bid Taka 9,65,000.00 for the cattle market and again at the direction of the authority increased it and deposited an amount of Taka 9,75,500.00. He has also argued that though there is a requirement for submitting sealed tender but there is nothing in law making unsealed tender invalid, it can at best be called irregular. He has argued that the question of submitting unsealed tender by the petitioner was not raised before the Deputy Commissioner, but was found for the first time in the order of the Additional Deputy, Commissioner. Therefore, the petitioner has followed all the rules for submitting tender and there is no breach of tender procedure for cancelling the lease agreement. Lastly, he argued that the tender money was raised to Taka 9,75,500.00 only at the direction of the authority and there was no negotiation between the petitioner and the authority to refix the bid amount. Dr. Rahman has submitted that the appellate authority should have been governed by the legality and not by public interest only, the reason for which the lease was cancelled. 

 11. Mr Abdur Razzaq has further submitted. that even before the inception of the lease agreement the whole tender procedure was vitiated by mala fide acts from certain quarter and therefore the lease agreement has lost its legal validity. In this connection he has referred to 39 DLR (AD) L whee in it has been held that power conferred by or under any law must not be exercised malafide or for collateral purpose. A malafide act is without jurisdiction. He has then drawn our attention to the negotiation between the authority and the petitioner to raise the bid money to Taka 9;75,000.00 which, according to him, is not permitted by law. He then attacked the tender agreement on tlte ground that it was not a sealed tender though the requirement of law under 2(Ka) of the aforesaid Rules is that for leasing of Hat and Bazar, sealed tenders Should be submitted. The learned Advocate further submits mat in view of the tender being not sealed and illegal negotiation taking place after the opening of the tender, the petitioner did not acquire any inchoate right for the protection of which he can come before this Court. He has further submitted that to come before this Court the petitioner must have an inchoate right. Lastly, he has contended that there was no violation of principle of natural-justice as the petitioner was heard by the Additional Divisional Commissioner before whom he had full opportunity to place his case. 

 18. Lastly, the Rule was issued challenging the impugned order, which may be noted, is based on finding of facts. But in the writ petition itself the impugned order was not attacked on the ground that finding of facts are not based on material evidence or they are based on surmises or conjectures or erroneous in nature. This court will interfere with the findings of the appellate authority only if the finding of facts are not based on material evidence. We are also of the view that the appearance of the petitioner before the Additional Commissioner shows that he had notice and full opportunity to explain his case before the concerned authority. Therefore, the lease agreement executed was not a valid document creating right in favour of the petitioner as the whole tender procedure was vitiated at the very inception. In short, the lease deed was void ab initio, nothing to show that the petitioner's right accrued by law.
